_comment: battle-clarity U4 — sentences that only mean something because of what the player is looking at. Every fixture runs on `basin-focus` (Chimera Squad selected, the objective 'Hold Fallow Gate' drilled open) and every `expected` envelope names the RESOLVED thing: rule 10 tells the model to write the name it read out of `focus`, never the pronoun the player said. Two of them are the cases where the honest answer is NOT an order — a pronoun whose antecedent is a force cannot be a place, and a sentence with no antecedent at all refuses rather than guessing. The offline half of the same behaviour (which produces the pronoun and lets `nl-focus.ts` bind it) is covered in nl-client.test.ts and nl-focus.test.ts; these fixtures are what a scored eval run measures the MODEL against.

fixtures.name: "defend it" with an objective drilled — the objective's place, not its title

expected.say: Chimera Squad is defending Fallow Gate.

fixtures.name: "pull them back to Osprey Fen" — a subject pronoun is the selection
fixtures.utterance: pull them back to Osprey Fen

expected.say: Chimera Squad is pulling back to Osprey Fen.

fixtures.name: "attack that town" — the pronoun wins over the name hiding inside it

expected.say: Chimera Squad is attacking Fallow Gate.

fixtures.name: "show me that" — a camera pronoun goes to the same place, and commits nothing
a pronoun whose antecedent is a FORCE is not a place — refuse, by name

actions.reason: "Chimera Squad" is one of your forces, not a place — name where you want them to defend.
